classification.difficultyReason: Read the centre from the diagram, calculate the radius gradient, apply the supplied perpendicular-tangent hint, and form and rearrange the line equation through the contact point.

content.prompt: Find the equation of the line that is tangent to the circle below at the point $(3,4)$. Express your answer in the form $ax+by=c$. Hint: The tangent to the circle will be perpendicular to the radius at this point.

spec.description: Origin-centred unfilled circle, descending tangent and marked contact point. Axes have arrowheads, titles and no numeric ticks. Circle and tangent retain distinct standard accent colours.
spec.mathematics: The circle is centred at (0,0) and passes through (3,4), so its radius is 5. The tangent is drawn from the derived equation 3x+4y=25, without printing that equation.
spec.answerVisibility: The contact point is a supplied given. No radius, gradient, equation or solution-only construction is printed.

answer.worked:
The centre is $(0,0)$, so the radius has gradient $m_r=\frac{4}{3}$. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius, hence $m_t=-\frac{3}{4}$.

$$\begin{align*}y-4&=-\frac{3}{4}(x-3)\\4y-16&=-3(x-3)\\4y-16&=-3x+9\\3x+4y&=25.\end{align*}$$
